title: Trump rallies in deep-red Alabama to 'thank' loyal voters as GOP eyes a key House seat
text:

Stated Claim / Post Context:
Trump rallies in deep-red Alabama to 'thank' loyal voters as GOP eyes a key House seat

Trump rallied in Mobile, Alabama, Friday in the latest stop on a swing through red states to boost election turnout among Republican voters, amid low approval ratings.

Actual Article Body:
His visit came amid low national approval ratings.

Fresh off his visit to Texas and Oklahoma, President Donald Trump rallied supporters in Mobile, Alabama, on Friday night. It was the latest stop on a swing through deep-red states to boost midterm election turnout among Republican voters and thank them for their support, amid low approval ratings for the president.

Trump said he he wanted to "pay respect" to his supporters and announced plans to return to the state next week for the Georgia-Alabama college football game.

In his remarks, Trump touted the economy, defended the Iran war and again told voters to pretend that he is on the ballot.

"When I'm not on the ballot, we don't do well. ... When I'm on the ballot, we kill everybody," he said. "So just close your eyes and pretend I'm on the ballot."

Actual Article Body:
A famed Florida restaurant whose owner pledged loyalty to Donald Trump is now struggling with empty tables as the president’s immigration crackdown keeps customers away, The Bulwark reported Friday.

“People are scared to come out and visit. When we make specials, sometimes we have to throw them out because they go bad,” an employee of El Arepazo told The Bulwark’s Adrian Carrasquillo, estimating a roughly 80% drop in business.

Just seven months ago, owner Maximo Alvarez welcomed Trump to the restaurant in Doral — home of the MAGA leader’s Trump National Doral Miami resort — with open arms, telling him, “I just want to be loyal to you.”

But according to The Bulwark, that loyalty didn’t get him too far.
